sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau, 2023 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances, individual unit file
DE Department of Elections, Campaign Finance Reporting System: contributions to New Castle County's local candidates since 2023

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2023 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts contributions from businesses, unions, PACs and non-profits to candidates for county council (or levy court), county executive and the other elected county offices, reported to the Department of Elections since 2023, classified by the contributor type each committee reports. Delaware allows business contributions. Individuals, candidates' own money and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, and New Castle County provides many other services; residents pay the city, the county and the school district.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money is not scored: no candidates for city council or commission and mayor reported contributions to the Department of Elections since 2023 (municipal candidates who raise and spend $5,000 or less do not file reports).
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
